title.en: The human eye, its defects and their correction
The girl who could not read the board

text.en: A girl in the last bench could read her book easily but could not read the blackboard, while her grandfather could read the board but needed to hold his newspaper far away. Both have a defect of vision, but of opposite kinds.

The eyeball is nearly spherical, about 2.3 cm across, and the tough outer membrane is the sclera.
Light enters through the transparent cornea, which is the main refracting surface, then passes through the pupil, whose size is controlled by the coloured iris.
The convex eye lens focuses a real and inverted image on the retina, and the optic nerve carries the signal to the brain, which sees it erect.
The ability of the eye to focus both near and far objects is the power of accommodation, done by the ciliary muscles changing the focal length of the lens.
To see a distant object the ciliary muscles relax and the lens becomes thinner; for a near object they contract and the lens becomes thicker.
A normal eye sees clearly between the near point at 25 cm and the far point at infinity.
Persistence of vision means that two light pulses less than one second apart cannot be seen separately, which is why a film appears to move.
In myopia the eyeball is too long, the far point comes closer and the image of distant objects forms in front of the retina; a concave lens corrects it.
In hypermetropia the eyeball is too short, the near point moves farther and the image of near objects forms behind the retina; a convex lens corrects it.
The power of a lens in dioptre is 1 divided by its focal length in metre, positive for convex and negative for concave lenses.

problem.en: A hypermetropic person has a near point at 50 cm and wants to read a book kept at 25 cm. Find the focal length and the power of the lens needed.

text.en: The lens must form a virtual image of the book at the person's near point. So u = -25 cm and v = -50 cm.

why.en: Sign convention: both on the object side.

text.en: So f = +50 cm = +0.5 m, a convex lens.

prompt.en: Compare myopia and hypermetropia: cause, what is seen clearly, and the lens used.

requiredIdeas.en: Myopia: eyeball too long, near clear, concave lens
Hypermetropia: eyeball too short, far clear, convex lens
Accommodation is done by the ciliary muscles

commonMisconceptions.en: Myopia is corrected by a convex lens
Both defects blur the same distance

points.en: Normal near point 25 cm and far point infinity.
Myopia: concave lens; hypermetropia: convex lens.
Ciliary muscles change the focal length of the lens (accommodation).
P = 1 / f (f in metre) in dioptre.
